Summary: No code-level regression exists between fireweed v0.31.10 (d206719b)
and the v0.31.14-successor pin (46bdaa6d == this worktree's HEAD, 9c9c342d —
zero code diff). The verification_command proves two things deterministically:
(1) HEAD is source-identical to the v0.31.14 tag the bead names, and (2) the
crates that implement the sqlite backend's claim/commit hot path
(fireweed-sqlite, fireweed-core, fireweed-relational, and the
ClaimPort/CommitTransitionPort impls in
fireweed-engine/src/async_log_replay_product.rs) are byte-for-byte unchanged
between v0.31.10 and v0.31.14. The bead's repro uses --backend sqlite, which
never executes the objectlog-only code the bead names as top suspect
(472b6ae3/2be7894a/6fcc28a8 recomposition chain — all #[cfg(feature =
"objectlog")]-gated or invoked only at process-open/rebuild, never on the
per-commit path).

Direct confirmation: built snorri-loadgen release binaries from both named
commits (snorri@6cc4c0fe1 pinning fireweed v0.31.10, and snorri@6814482eb
pinning fireweed v0.31.14 == this HEAD) and ran them interleaved, 4 paired
trials, exact repro command from the bead. Mean deltas were claim_transition
+0.1%, dispatch -3.9%, enroll -4.6% — within this host's own run-to-run noise
band (individual dispatch samples ranged 2,348-3,906 items/s), not the
one-directional -15%/-45% the bead reports. ps aux during the investigation
showed >5 concurrent claude/ddx agent processes actively running other beads
on this shared host, including one inside the snorri checkout itself, which
better explains the original single-sample A/B's asymmetry than a code
regression the diff evidence rules out.

No fireweed source was changed. The six objectlog recomposition tests and
159/159 snorri adapter suite are unaffected (nothing in their dependency
surface was touched); they were already validated against this exact code at
commit a5a18a5c earlier in this history.

Recommendation for the next attempt if this regression resurfaces: benchmark
on a host with verified-exclusive access (e.g. gate on `pgrep -f 'claude|ddx
work|cargo build'` returning empty, not just load average < 2.5), since a
1-minute load average is too coarse to catch fsync-bound contention from
sibling agent sessions on this shared box.
